Q134285876.summary: Within an acanthus border, Christ hangs on the cross beneath the INRI title, his head inclined and his feet resting on a footrest. The Virgin raises her hands in sorrow at the left, and John, holding a book, stands at the right. The quiet, balanced composition reflects the restrained dignity of German ivory carving in the 11th century.
facts: The pairing of the Virgin and John beneath the cross recalls Christ's words entrusting his mother to the beloved disciple.
Q134285876.notes: Little published information was found beyond Wikidata and the Commons file (Germany, 11th century, ivory).
Q134285876.original_title: Christus am Kreuz zwischen Maria und Johannes

cur:monumental-santa-prassede-zeno-chris.summary: Within a niche framed by bands of colour, a bearded Christ holding a jewelled book stands at the centre between two haloed saints, shown half-length against a gold ground. The frontal, solemn figures, with large dark eyes and strongly outlined features, are typical of the mosaic style of Paschal I's Rome.
facts: The Chapel of Saint Zeno was built by Pope Paschal I (817–824) as a funerary chapel for his mother, Theodora; its walls and vault are almost entirely clad in gold-ground mosaic.
Paschal I's mosaics belong to the Carolingian-era revival in Rome, when the pope also translated many martyrs' relics from the catacombs into the city's churches.

links.label: Wikimedia Commons: Basilica of Saint Praxedes (Rome) - Jesus Christ between two saints mosaic

cur:monumental-santa-prassede-zeno-chris.notes: The flanking saints are identified variously; the Flickr source names them as Paschal and Valentinus, Commons also suggests Valentinus and Zeno.

cur:monumental2-tokali-christ-enthroned.summary: Christ sits frontally on a high-backed jewelled throne with a cushion, a large cross-inscribed halo behind his head, holding a richly bound Gospel book on his knee and raising his right hand in blessing. Much of the paint of the face and mantle has worn away, but the monumental pose of the Ruler of All remains clear.
facts: Enthroned images of Christ holding the Gospel book were often placed in apses or flanked by the Virgin and John the Baptist in a Deesis, as intercession for the faithful.
cur:monumental2-tokali-christ-enthroned.notes: The photograph is labelled only 'Christ Pantocrator scene'; its exact position within Tokalı Kilise (Old or New Church) was not verified, so a general 10th-century date is given.

walters:W.432.63V.summary: In the upper miniature, Christ stands bound on a raised, columned porch beside Pilate, who gestures toward the crowd below; the people shout and raise their arms, demanding Barabbas instead. In the lower one, Christ, stripped and covered with wounds, is beaten by two tormentors, one with a bundle of birch rods, while in the background figures press the crown of thorns onto his head. The two images follow the Gospel text between them, from 'Non hunc sed Barabbam' to the scourging and crowning.
facts: The page carries two miniatures, 9 and 5 lines high, illustrating John 18:38–40 and John 19:1–16.
The prayer book was made in Leiden in the first quarter of the 16th century.

walters:W.432.63V.notes: Origin in Leiden and the date 1500–1525 follow the Walters manuscript description (TEI, The Digital Walters). The worklist year (800) was a parsing error for '1st quarter 16th century'. The Walters title 'The Jews Release Barabbas Instead of Christ' is replaced with a more neutral descriptive title.
